title: Projection-defined constant-tower derived-limit unit
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme and $A,I,A_T$ an adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(A_T)$ and $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-inverse-system]. Let $\Delta$ be the exact constant-tower functor and $\Delta_D$ its termwise derived functor [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian, lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Use the derived localizations $Q_{\mathcal A},Q_{\operatorname{Tow}}$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Fix a functorial K-injective tower resolution $\iota_M:M\to J(M)$, with K-injective meaning that maps from acyclic tower complexes are null-homotopic [def-pur-kinjective-complex], and let $\mathcal L=R\lim$ be its total derived inverse-limit functor [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality]. For a complex $C$ the components of $\iota_{\Delta C}$ factor uniquely through the ordinary degreewise inverse limit, giving $z_C:C\to\lim_nJ(\Delta C)_n$ with $\pi_nz_C=(\iota_{\Delta C})_n$.
Under the fixed localization comparisons $Q_{\mathcal A}(\lim J(\Delta C))\cong\mathcal L\Delta_D(Q_{\mathcal A}C)$, the maps $Q_{\mathcal A}(z_C)$ descend to a natural transformation
$$\eta:\mathrm{id}_{D(\mathcal A)}\longrightarrow\mathcal L\Delta_D.$$
For every derived morphism $h:C\to D$ one has $\mathcal L\Delta_D(h)\eta_C=\eta_Dh$. This is the projection-defined constant-tower map specified in [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], without a choice of a morphism between unrelated triangulated cones.

proof.text: For a tower complex $M$, write $H(M)=\lim_nJ(M)_n$, taken degreewise. The module-sheaf limit theorem supplies these limits, computed as compatible families of sections. The differential sends $(x_n)_n$ to $(d x_n)_n$; transitions are chain maps, so this remains a compatible family and its differential squares to zero. If $u:M\to N$ is a tower chain map, set $H(u)((x_n)_n)=(J(u)_n(x_n))_n$. These maps commute with the differential. Functoriality of the fixed $J$ gives $H(1)=1$ and $H(vu)=H(v)H(u)$ componentwise. Thus $H$ is a functor on tower complexes, without requiring exactness of inverse limits.

source.place: Agent expansion of the completed-pullback invocation; ordinary limits: Stacks sites-modules.tex, Tag 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits) and Tag 03CO (lemma-limits-colimits-abelian-sheaves), part (2).

proof.text: For every complex $C$, put $a_{C,n}=(\iota_{\Delta C})_n:C\to J(\Delta C)_n$. Since $\iota_{\Delta C}$ is a morphism of towers and the transitions of $\Delta C$ are identities, $t_n a_{C,n+1}=a_{C,n}$. Hence $z_C(x)=(a_{C,n}(x))_n$ is a section of $H(\Delta C)$ in each degree. It commutes with restriction and is $A_T$-linear. Each $a_{C,n}$ is a chain map, so $d z_C(x)=(d a_{C,n}(x))_n=(a_{C,n}(dx))_n=z_C(dx)$. Its projections are precisely $a_{C,n}$. Any other such chain map agrees on all coordinates, hence equals $z_C$.

source.place: Agent expansion: factor the compatible component maps of the fixed resolution through the ordinary inverse limit.

proof.text: Let $f:C\to D$ be a chain map. Naturality of the stipulated resolution transformation $\iota$ gives $J(\Delta f)_n a_{C,n}=a_{D,n}f$ for every $n$. Therefore, writing $\pi_{D,n}:H(\Delta D)\to J(\Delta D)_n$, one has $\pi_{D,n}H(\Delta f)z_C=J(\Delta f)_n a_{C,n}=a_{D,n}f=\pi_{D,n}z_Df$. The coordinate description of the limit makes its projections jointly monic, so $H(\Delta f)z_C=z_Df$. Thus $z$ is a natural transformation on the category of complexes. No additivity of the resolution functor is needed for this calculation.

source.place: Agent expansion: naturality checked on every resolution projection.

proof.text: Exactness in the tower category is levelwise. A short exact sequence sent through $\Delta$ is the same short exact sequence at every level, so $\Delta$ is exact. The exact-functor factorization theorem therefore gives the natural comparison $Q_{\operatorname{Tow}}\Delta\cong\Delta_D Q_{\mathcal A}$. Set $B=Q_{\mathcal A}H\Delta$ and $G=\mathcal L\Delta_D$. The stipulated localization comparisons for the total derived inverse-limit functor computed by this same $J$ give a natural isomorphism $\beta:B\xrightarrow{\sim}GQ_{\mathcal A}$, by composing $Q_{\mathcal A}H\cong\mathcal LQ_{\operatorname{Tow}}$ with the preceding comparison. These are comparisons of functors, including their maps, rather than arbitrary isomorphisms of their object values. In particular $B$ inverts quasi-isomorphisms: for such an $s$, $\beta_D B(s)=G(Q_{\mathcal A}(s))\beta_C$, whose right side is invertible.

source.place: Agent expansion: the fixed derived-localization comparisons; the total derived inverse-limit functor is the one already provided by prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality.

proof.text: Apply $Q_{\mathcal A}$ to the natural transformation in Step 3 and then compose with $\beta$. This gives $\tau:Q_{\mathcal A}\Rightarrow GQ_{\mathcal A}$ with $\tau_C=\beta_C Q_{\mathcal A}(z_C)$. Both functors invert quasi-isomorphisms, and $Q_{\mathcal A}$ is localization at precisely that class. Apply clause (2) of the localization universal-property theorem with source $\mathrm{CoCh}(\mathcal A)$, target $D(\mathcal A)$, $F_1=Q_{\mathcal A}$, $F_2=GQ_{\mathcal A}$ and descended functors $F_1^{\prime}=\mathrm{id}$, $F_2^{\prime}=G$. It produces the unique natural transformation $\eta:\mathrm{id}\Rightarrow G$ with $\eta_{Q_{\mathcal A}C}=\tau_C$. This proves descent from complexes and covers every derived morphism, including inverses of quasi-isomorphisms, without an assumption that derived morphisms lift to chain maps.

source.place: Agent expansion: descent of a natural transformation through localization; the cited localization node supplies the natural-transformation clause (Mathlib Localization.liftNatTrans), not merely factorization of functors.

proof.text: Naturality of the descended transformation now gives $\mathcal L\Delta_D(h)\eta_C=\eta_Dh$ for every $h:C\to D$ in $D(\mathcal A)$. The constant-tower map in the completed-pullback definition is specified by taking the tower resolution $\Delta C\to J(\Delta C)$ and factoring its compatible maps into the ordinary inverse limit. Step 2 is exactly this factorization, and Step 5 has component $\beta_CQ_{\mathcal A}(z_C)$ under the fixed comparisons. Thus it is that specified map, with its naturality now established. Uniqueness in Step 2 concerns the ordinary limit of complexes; no claim that projections determine arbitrary maps into a triangulated homotopy limit is used.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q28-555d88a58 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS. This is a one-commit split of the item into six steps, with no new nodes. The statement is byte-identical to the live node, the live item is still unsplit, and the item has no repair note and is not on any dropped list. I read every cited statement in full. The specified map is exactly the one prescribed in def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback: take a tower K-injective resolution and factor its components through lim I_n. Steps 1-3 build H = lim J degreewise and the map z_C using the module-limit leaf (Stacks 03DB/03CO), the tower-morphism condition with identity transitions, and naturality of ι. Joint monicity of the projections gives naturality on complexes. Step 4: Δ is exact because exactness is levelwise. β is the composite of the exact-functor comparison with the fixed comparison Q_A H ≅ Rlim Q_Tow for the same J (prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality). Because β is natural, B inverts quasi-isomorphisms. Step 5 applies localization clause (2) with F1 = Q_A, F2 = G Q_A, F1' = id and F2' = G; I checked this against Mathlib liftNatTrans_app. Step 6 reads off the specification. The parent's Step 7 uses exactly this derived-morphism naturality. The coefficient category is Mod(A_T) with completed coefficients, and no η-iso claim is made. Small cases checked: C = 0, an acyclic C, a single-degree C, the identity map and empty T. The cited Stacks tags 079P, 03DB, 03CO and 04VG are verified, and no SGA is cited. No duplicates were found in a grep of all constant-tower nodes; the adjunction-unit nodes use a different construction. There are no cycles. I accept the declared tool use of prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality, from unit sk-thm-properbasechange, as a generic Rlim functor that replaces no CBC route step. Advisory only: tower K-injectivity cites def-pur-kinjective-complex, which is stated for modules on a site, but the item spells the meaning out inline. Review written to review.md; no fixes.
